title: UAP Disclosure Act controlled disclosure campaign plan and records review board

tellings.difference: Told firsthand by Schumer, crediting Rounds, and draws the comparison with the JFK assassination records board.
tellings.link_reason: Schumer describes the records review board, modelled on the JFK board, that the UAP Disclosure Act would create, which is the same as the records-review-board story.

plain: A proposed US law called the UAP Disclosure Act, where UAP means unidentified anomalous phenomena, the official term for UFOs, would have set up a review board to release government records on the subject. The researcher Matthew Pines describes a "controlled disclosure campaign plan," credited to a man named Karl Nell, under which this board would have the standing of a government agency, the power to order people to testify, and the power to declassify records itself, with the president able to overrule it. Senator Chuck Schumer, who backed the bill, speaks of it himself in a clip Michels plays. He says the measure he championed with Senator Mike Rounds "would create a board just like we did with the JFK assassination records," meaning the panel that released files on President Kennedy's killing. A related story says the review panel was later taken out of the bill. It is told because such a board would force secret records into public view.
